what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted 5-2 to impose the agent's recommended fine for cutting in the no-touch buffer zone at 667/675 Reservoir Road.
It issued a negative determination 4-3 for the 171 Lancaster Ave pillars, same size, with a waiver and subject to Selectmen approval.
Enforcement orders for 225 Pleasant Street and 190 Electric Ave were extended to September 21.
Negative determinations also passed for 150 Peninsula Drive and 44 Brookview Terrace; the 83 West Street hearing was continued to September 7.
The commission elected a chairman, vice chair and clerk, and set an extra regulatory review meeting for August 31.

why_it_matters: Fines and enforcement orders show how the commission applies wetland buffer rules to private property owners, and a split vote on the town-land pillars shows the commission was divided on that decision.
The Lancaster Ave pillar decision depends on a Selectmen approval that has not yet been given, and the regulatory review may change the rules that apply to future projects near wetlands.
watch_next: September 7 agenda: continued hearings for 83 West Street, 667/675 Reservoir Road and the 178 Peninsula Drive extension, plus the trail ride request and policy review.
August 31 regulatory review meeting, and the September 21 expiry of the extended enforcement orders.

meetings.headline: Commission ordered a positive determination at 7 Ruth Street, denying new sand on a beach; approved Summer Street DPW project.
meetings.summary: The Conservation Commission heard several requests for determination and notices of intent. It denied sand for a lakefront beach at 7 Ruth Street, allowing a mowed vegetated area with a recorded agreement, and approved the Summer Street road project and the Northfield Road homes with conditions. Enforcement matters were pushed to administrative hearings on July 6, and a departing member was thanked.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted a positive determination for 7 Ruth Street, so new sand on the beach is not allowed; the area may revegetate with mowing under a recorded agreement.
The commission unanimously approved the Summer Street DPW road project plans with a standard order of conditions.
The Northfield Road notice of intent was approved with conditions, including driveway pads and sweeping, a staked 50-foot no-touch line, erosion control and individual lot plans.
Enforcement at 101 Pleasant Street was continued to July 6, with a remediation plan due then; administrative hearings were added for three other enforcement matters.
Negative determinations were voted for the Sunset Lane wall, Chase Road buffer planting, Laurel Lane dock (held for Chapter 91 approval) and Spring Street screenhouse.

why_it_matters: The 7 Ruth Street vote and the Northfield Road conditions show how the commission limits work near water and wetlands on private lots, which bears on what neighbors may build or alter.
The Summer Street road project and the Hollis Road deck quotes may draw on town funds, and the commission asked for a check with the accounting office on the deck quotes.
watch_next: July 6 meeting: 7 Ruth Street agreement signing, the 101 Pleasant Street remediation plan, and administrative hearings for 190 Electric Ave, Howard Street and Hemlock.
Chapter 91 approval for the 100 Laurel Lane dock, after which the determination is to be signed.
